bugs.error_message: Registry root-distribution check reported "outside /mnt/j/projectshome: 0" when the true answer is 2; extraction had silently yielded 0 paths.
bugs.root_cause: Ad-hoc verification one-liner extracted registry paths with `x.path || x.dir`, but registry entries use the `root` key. Zero paths extracted meant zero survived the filter, and an empty filter result was read as a substantive negative finding. Same vacuous-zero class as bug-066 (grep -L on a non-matching glob), reproduced in the check written to replace it.
bugs.fix: Reordered extraction to prefer `root`, and added a fail-closed guard: if extracted path count != registry entry count, exit 2 refusing to report coverage. Falsified with a schema-drift registry ({location:...} entries) which now exits 2 instead of passing.

bugs.error_message: Fleet coverage verifier passed on a project whose section heading was intact but whose BODY had been reverted to a superseded rule.
bugs.root_cause: Coverage was asserted with body.includes(<heading>). Heading presence is a propagation signal, not a content signal, so stale/partial/reverted section bodies verified as covered. Raised by an external reviewer (Finding 8); the reviewer predicted heading REMOVAL would also pass, which was false (measured: MISSING named the project), but the content case was real.
bugs.fix: Extract the canonical section from src/templates/OPENWOLF.md, normalize (CRLF, trailing WS) and sha256 it, compare per project, report drifted=<n> naming each, and fail unless drifted==0. Falsified by corrupting one real fleet project body: heading-only check PASS -> content-bound check FAIL naming the project; restored byte-identical after.

bugs.error_message: verify-fleet-section.mjs printed RESULT: PASS while performing only heading-presence checks when run from any cwd other than the repo root.
bugs.root_cause: Canonical template resolved with path.join(process.cwd(),"src/templates/OPENWOLF.md"). From another cwd the template was not found, canonical stayed null, and the script degraded to the heading-only check bug-692 had just eliminated — then reported PASS. Found by exercising the staged canary rule before fleet propagation.
bugs.fix: Resolve template relative to the script via fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), and fail closed (exit 2) when no canonical section can be bound, with an explicit --allow-unbound override. Falsified: run from /tmp now content-binds and PASSes; a section absent from the template exits 2 instead of reporting coverage.

bugs.error_message: learning.explicit nudge misfired twice (learning-c2405746, learning-f7b7ade9) on turns that relay a third-party review or announce a handoff document, classifying them as user corrections for ## Do-Not-Repeat.
bugs.root_cause: The correction pattern matches bare never/always/don't anywhere in the turn. Role filtering was NOT the problem (readRecentUserTurns already restricts to entry.type===user); the problem is that a user turn quoting an assistant ship report or reviewer verdict is user bytes carrying directive tokens. The existing quotation guard was ^-anchored on here's/quoted/example only, so attribution prefixes and document-report openers were uncovered. Review-pipeline prose is maximally dense in these tokens.
bugs.fix: Added a ^-anchored RELAY guard covering attribution prefixes and document-report openers. Both misfire texts now classify null; all true positives preserved, including a genuine correction that mentions a handoff document. Regression test added; 190/190 pass. Deployed hook copies synced fleet-wide and verified behaviourally.

bugs.error_message: openwolf driftcheck reported 221 of 222 anatomy entries missing, including files that demonstrably exist (src/cli/index.ts)
bugs.root_cause: Anatomy section headings are project-root-relative ("## src/cli/"), but entries were resolved with path.resolve(wolfDir, rel), producing <root>/.wolf/src/cli/index.ts. Every real file therefore reported missing.
bugs.fix: Resolve anatomy entries against the project root: path.resolve(root, rel). Regression test "anatomy entries resolve against the project root, not .wolf/" fails if the base regresses.

bugs.error_message: Anatomy entries appearing before the first ## heading were dropped without being counted, shrinking the coverage denominator invisibly
bugs.root_cause: `if (!e || section === null) continue` skipped unresolvable entries BEFORE incrementing extracted, so an entry that could not be checked simply vanished from the count. The vacuity guard (extracted === checked) could not catch it because both stayed consistent — the same defect class the command exists to detect.
bugs.fix: Count every matched entry before resolving; report a section-less entry as anatomy-missing with an explicit "(entry precedes any section heading)" detail. Found by a unit test asserting the denominator, not by inspection.

bugs.error_message: Negative-control harness printed exit=0 for controls that had correctly failed
bugs.root_cause: Controls were run as `node ... driftcheck --check 2>&1 | grep -E ...; echo exit=$?`. In a pipeline $? is the LAST command's status, so every control reported grep's exit code (0) instead of the checker's. The controls looked like they proved the check cannot fail.
bugs.fix: Measure exit status directly with output redirected to a file, never through a pipe. Verified: drift=1, vacuous=1, clean=0.

bugs.error_message: driftcheck reported 4/4 false positives on a hand-written anatomy: existing README.md/CLAUDE.md flagged missing, and brace-notation filenames never matched
bugs.root_cause: Two assumptions failed on hand-written indexes: (1) section headings are always directory paths, but prose headings like "## Top level" were joined as directories; (2) entries are always literal filenames, but "koch_1904_{wikipedia,mactutor}.txt" is brace notation for two files. Also the entry regex only matched backtick format, so a bold-format anatomy extracted 0 entries and tripped the vacuity guard.
bugs.fix: sectionDir() resolves whitespace-bearing (prose) headings to the project root; expandBraces() expands sibling notation and requires every variant to exist; ANATOMY_ENTRY accepts both `name` and **name**. The vacuity guard is what surfaced the format blindness rather than a false clean pass.

bugs.error_message: driftcheck reported .wolf/qa/.wolf/qa/<file>.md missing — a doubled path prefix for files that exist
bugs.root_cause: Anatomy entries are inconsistent: some are bare names relative to their heading ("index.ts" under "## src/cli/"), others already carry the full project-root-relative path (".wolf/qa/x.md" under "## .wolf/qa/"). Unconditional join(section, name) doubled the prefix for the second form. 150 of 411 mt5automation findings were this class.
bugs.fix: Resolve against the section base OR the project root; only an entry satisfying neither is drift. Guarded by a paired test asserting the fallback still fails on a file absent under both bases, so the extra leniency cannot make the check unfalsifiable.

bugs.error_message: driftcheck hung past 30s on dependency-heavy projects; 43 of 85 fleet projects returned no parseable output
bugs.root_cause: The parked-question check walked every source file to depth 8 unconditionally, even in the overwhelmingly common case where no parked-questions ledger exists and the walk result is discarded. 39s on one project. A session-end check that hangs is a check that does not get run.
bugs.fix: Skip the walk when no ledger exists and say so explicitly in the SKIP text ("code not scanned for orphan TODO(UQ-n) markers") rather than emitting a bare "no parked questions" that implies a scan. Walk is additionally capped at 20000 files, reporting VACUOUS on truncation instead of silently returning partial coverage. 39s -> 3.7s.

bugs.error_message: Fleet drift scan reported "455 stale across 10 projects" while 43 of 85 projects had silently failed to produce output
bugs.root_cause: Per-project results were aggregated without asserting that the number of projects successfully checked equalled the registry count. Projects that timed out contributed nothing and were invisible in the totals, so a half-fleet sample read as a fleet result.
bugs.fix: Assert checked === roots.length and emit an explicit WARN naming the shortfall and parse-error count. The guard is what exposed the timeout defect (bug-700); without it the partial numbers would have been reported as fleet-wide truth.

bugs.error_message: driftcheck reported a deleted file as clean: anatomy entry "auth.ts" under "## src/api/" resolved against an unrelated auth.ts at the project root
bugs.root_cause: The root fallback added for bug-699 (entries carrying their own section prefix) was applied UNCONDITIONALLY. Any entry could therefore resolve against a same-named file anywhere the root candidate landed, so a genuinely deleted/moved file was rescued by a basename collision — the exact stale-entry class the command exists to detect. Generic basenames (index.ts, config.ts, README.md) make the collision ordinary rather than exotic. The existing regression test did not cover it: docs/nowhere.md was absent under BOTH candidate paths, so it proved only that the fallback cannot rescue a name absent everywhere — a strictly weaker claim that a single-base implementation would also satisfy.
bugs.fix: Gate the root fallback on selfPrefixed: the entry must literally begin with its own section path. Verified by negative control — reverting the guard turns the new collision test red (exit=1) and restoring it returns 17/17. bug-699 confirmed still fixed on real mt5automation data (0 doubled-prefix false positives). Surfaced 26 previously-hidden stale entries on that project alone (360 -> 386), 8 of 8 spot-checked as genuinely absent.

bugs.error_message: `openwolf experiment evidence --metric acc=` silently recorded a metric value of 0
bugs.root_cause: Number("") returns 0 in JS, so an empty metric value parsed as a real-looking zero reading instead of erroring. A missing measurement became a data point.
bugs.fix: parseMetric() rejects an empty value before calling Number(), so a missing metric is an error rather than a silent 0.

bugs.error_message: driftcheck reported phantom orphan TODO(UQ-7) markers that did not exist in real source
bugs.root_cause: The source walker read test fixture strings containing TODO(UQ-n) literals as if they were real markers in production code.
bugs.fix: listCodeFiles excludes test dirs and *.test.*/*.spec.* files, mirroring the quality gate's own scope definition.

bugs.error_message: Skill installs accepted SKILL.md frontmatter whose description named a specific vendor, silently narrowing the skill's trigger surface
bugs.root_cause: validateSkill only checked the frontmatter `name:`. The `description:` is the routing surface Claude matches against user requests; provider-specific wording means the skill never fires for equivalent generic phrasing, with no error emitted.
bugs.fix: validateSkill extracts description (quoted/unquoted/block-scalar forms), rejects missing or empty ones, and warns on provider-specific wording via providerWordingHits().

bugs.error_message: Bare `openwolf update` deployed template changes to all 84 registered projects when a single-project canary was intended
bugs.root_cause: `openwolf update` is fleet-wide by DEFAULT (src/cli/update.ts:2, `let selected = allProjects` at line 102). Scope narrows only when --project is passed; there is no bare-vs---all distinction. Running it from inside a project directory does NOT scope it to that project -- cwd is irrelevant to targeting. The Staged Rollout section mandates canary-first deployment but names no command that actually achieves it, so following the rule literally still produces a fleet write.
bugs.fix: Use `openwolf update --project <name>` for canary deployment. Documented the scoping flag in the Staged Rollout section of the protocol template so the rule names the mechanism that satisfies it. verify-fleet-section.mjs gained --only <root> to verify a single canary project without fleet staleness masking the result; --only fails closed when the target is unregistered rather than reporting PASS over zero projects.

bugs.error_message: Buglog auto-detect merged two DIFFERENT files' fixes into one entry when they shared a basename
bugs.root_cause: autoDetectBugFix's duplicate-suppression predicate compared path.basename(b.file) against the edited file's basename, while the comment above it stated 'same file + same category'. relFile -- the value actually stored as b.file -- was computed 7 lines earlier and left unused. This repo has 21 basenames shared by 2+ tracked files (TS/JS/template triads), so the collision is the dominant editing pattern, not an edge case.
bugs.fix: Compare the full project-relative path (b.file !== relFile) in all four copies: src/hooks/post-write.ts, src/hooks/post-write.js, .wolf/hooks/post-write.js, templates/wolf/hooks/post-write.js. Added tests/post-write-dedup-path.test.js pinning both directions (distinct files separate, same file still dedupes).

bugs.error_message: Interrupted or killed Node test runs leave allowlisted OpenWolf fixture directories behind
bugs.root_cause: Fixture cleanup existed only in per-test finally blocks, which do not run after process interruption or forced termination; no bounded stale recovery existed for abandoned roots. The first stale-sweep implementation also trusted root mtime alone, allowing a live process older than 24 hours to be raced by another importer.
bugs.fix: Added an exact-prefix fixture helper with synchronous exit/SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup, 24-hour location-specific stale sweeping, and converted the leaking test call sites. Live roots now carry a PID owner marker and are retained when signal-zero probing confirms the owner is alive.

bugs.error_message: listPm2Processes() starts a PM2 God Daemon while performing a read-only query against an inactive PM2 home
bugs.root_cause: `pm2 jlist` starts PM2 when no daemon exists, and the listing path invoked it without first validating a live daemon PID.
bugs.fix: Resolve PM2 home, validate pm2.pid as a positive safe integer, probe it with signal zero (EPERM alive), and return [] before invoking PM2 when missing, malformed, or dead.

bugs.error_message: openwolf daemon start can disable dashboard mode on an existing dashboard-enabled PM2 daemon
bugs.root_cause: daemonStart calls ensurePm2Daemon without preserving the existing dashboard flag, so mode comparison restarts the process with dashboard disabled.
bugs.fix: Open review finding; preserve or explicitly document mode semantics before changing this pre-existing path.

bugs.error_message: cleanupOpenWolfPm2 with an injected process snapshot can restart PM2 after the daemon disappears
bugs.root_cause: The mutating cleanup path trusts a previously supplied snapshot and invokes pm2 delete/save without rechecking daemon liveness, leaving a TOCTOU side effect.
bugs.fix: Open review finding; add a pre-mutation liveness policy without weakening intended cleanup behavior.

bugs.error_message: legacy PM2 migration reports the deleted legacy name instead of the newly started hashed name
bugs.root_cause: ensurePm2Daemon starts the hashed name but returns and prints existingName from the deleted legacy registration.
bugs.fix: Open review finding; report the replacement name or explicit old-to-new migration wording.

bugs.error_message: Wolfpack CLI was not accessible by command name in WSL2 or PowerShell
bugs.root_cause: The current WSL NVM Node version had no global customopenwolf installation, while Windows retained a conflicting legacy openwolf@2.5.0 global package that provided only openwolf and blocked creation of this project's shims with EEXIST.
bugs.fix: Installed this repository globally into the WSL npm prefix; uninstalled the legacy Windows openwolf package and installed this repository globally into the Windows npm prefix, creating and verifying both wolfpack and openwolf aliases.

bugs.fix: Recomputed the retained-root totals from parsed metrics, corrected all stale counts and denominators, replaced the ambiguous root label with a stable descriptive label, and ran explicit stale-string plus retained-root manifest checks.

bugs.error_message: cron run reported success for a task ID that did not exist

bugs.error_message: Parallel read and SessionStart hooks silently lost session-state and ledger updates
bugs.root_cause: Atomic rename prevented torn JSON but did not serialize read-modify-write operations across hook processes.
bugs.fix: Added fail-closed lock-backed mutateJSON transactions and session-keyed state; concurrent regressions retain every update.

bugs.error_message: Parallel project registrations silently erased peers
bugs.root_cause: Registry writers read before locking and independently replaced valid snapshots.
bugs.fix: Moved registry read-modify-write inside a cross-process lock with strict atomic persistence and malformed-byte preservation.

bugs.error_message: Cron daemon and CLI processes could lose concurrent cron-state updates
bugs.root_cause: The module-local Promise queue serialized only one process; independent processes still raced on cron-state.json.
bugs.fix: Added cross-process locking, in-lock reads, strict atomic writes, and fail-closed malformed-state handling.

bugs.error_message: Malformed registry, cron state, hook state, or project config could be silently replaced with defaults
bugs.root_cause: Broad parse fallbacks treated existing malformed or unreadable bytes like a first-run ENOENT state.
bugs.fix: Restricted defaults to ENOENT and refuse mutation otherwise, preserving existing bytes for recovery.

bugs.error_message: Scanner reopened files for descriptions and leaked descriptors when reads failed
bugs.root_cause: The scanner already had file content but extractDescription opened the file again, and closeSync was not protected by finally.
bugs.fix: Accept supplied content, use the scanner single-read pipeline, and close independently opened descriptors in finally.

bugs.error_message: SessionStart cleanup deleted live lock-staging and atomic-write temporary files from concurrent hooks
bugs.root_cause: Every SessionStart unlinked every .tmp in .wolf without age or ownership checks.
bugs.fix: Only remove temporary files older than ten minutes; fresh in-flight files survive concurrent startup.

bugs.error_message: Hook packaging drift could omit runtime dependencies while hook commands swallowed import failures
bugs.root_cause: Init, update, status, templates, and verification maintained independent incomplete file and registration lists.
bugs.fix: Added one canonical manifest, exact payload copying, all-entry self-checks, transactional health state, and visible loader errors.

bugs.error_message: Keyed session state broke legacy sessions and direct lifecycle-hook fixtures
bugs.root_cause: A valid session ID always selected a new keyed path even when a matching legacy _session.json held the active state.
bugs.fix: Use a matching legacy state file when no keyed state exists, while SessionStart explicitly initializes new keyed state.

bugs.error_message: Live-only buglog audit misclassified intentional rolling-window archival as data loss
bugs.root_cause: The audit compared HEAD only to the live buglog and ignored `.wolf/archive/buglog-*.json`, even though size discipline intentionally moves expired records into monthly archives.

bugs.root_cause: The missing-hash guard emitted pending-review remediation before distinguishing a read-only check of a completed legacy receipt; completed receipts correctly reject refresh, so the guidance had no executable path.
bugs.fix: Keep exit 6 because drift cannot be proven without stored hashes, but emit completed-legacy-specific text with no refresh instruction and preserve exact reviewlog bytes.

bugs.error_message: complete-review accepted --check together with mutation flags and bypassed fail-closed hash validation
bugs.root_cause: Argument parsing independently enabled check and refresh/review provenance modes. Because refresh was true, the missing-hash guard was skipped before the earlier check branch exited, producing a false STALE verdict and impossible remediation.
bugs.fix: Reject --check combined with --refresh, --reviewed-current, or --reviewed-hash as usage exit 2 before review state is read.

bugs.error_message: complete-review --check ignored stored hash keys absent from review.files and could report CURRENT when completion reported STALE
bugs.root_cause: The read-only check compared only review.files, while completion also rejected keys present only in content_hashes. The two paths therefore disagreed on the same receipt.
bugs.fix: Compute mismatched and missing reviewed files once for both check and completion, include missing keys in check output, and return STALE exit 4.

bugs.error_message: Missing await
bugs.root_cause: The syntactic auto-detector classified a regression-test edit made for bug-778 and bug-779; the executable suite found no separate missing-await defect.
bugs.fix: Consolidated into bug-778 and bug-779.

bugs.error_message: Hook manifest membership and self-check tests could pass against stale dist bytes
bugs.root_cause: The regression imported the compiled dist manifest and executed dist hooks while behavior tests exercised source-adjacent hooks. A source edit without rebuild left the supposed source contract green against old bytes.
bugs.fix: Import the canonical source TypeScript manifest with Node native type stripping and execute source-adjacent hook JavaScript for membership and self-check; retain dist only for the unrelated nudge CLI discovery fixture.

bugs.error_message: Wrong condition in logic
bugs.root_cause: The syntactic auto-detector recorded each source/runtime side of the same refresh-mode exclusivity correction; neither is a separate defect.
bugs.fix: Consolidated into bug-785.

bugs.error_message: Wrong condition in logic
bugs.root_cause: The syntactic auto-detector recorded each source/runtime side of the same refresh-mode exclusivity correction; neither is a separate defect.
bugs.fix: Consolidated into bug-785.

bugs.error_message: Missing await
bugs.root_cause: The syntactic auto-detector classified async regression-fixture edits; the executable suite found no missing-await defect.
bugs.fix: Consolidated into bug-786.

bugs.error_message: complete-review silently discarded --reviewed-current when combined with --refresh
bugs.root_cause: Refresh mode rejected --reviewed-hash but not its sibling --reviewed-current attestation. The refresh branch won and exited successfully while leaving the review pending, so one supplied completion intent was silently ignored.
bugs.fix: Reject --refresh combined with either completion attestation as usage exit 2 before reading review state, and assert both combinations preserve exact reviewlog bytes.

bugs.error_message: covered-token basis regression test exercised a local algorithm copy instead of the shipped Stop hook
bugs.root_cause: The test mirrored advanceCoveredTokens in a local closure, so a regression in src/hooks/stop.ts could leave the test green. No hook-level fixture drove scoped-to-session fallback or session-to-scoped recovery.
bugs.fix: Replace the mirrored unit test with two end-to-end Stop-hook fixtures that persist opposite-basis pending reviews, drive both transitions through shipped runtime bytes, and assert the stored value and basis change together.

bugs.error_message: Oversized Read guard exclusion test incorrectly required no session state after exercising an admitted missing project path.
bugs.root_cause: The exclusion test combined paths that return before bookkeeping with a missing in-project path that existing pre-read semantics admit and record. It asserted that the keyed session file did not exist, so the first focused run failed even though the guard correctly emitted no denial.
bugs.fix: During the transient mechanism proof, the assertion was narrowed to the load-bearing empty guard marker while preserving admitted-attempt bookkeeping; the suite then passed 10/10 and both broken-code controls failed. The entire size-only canary and its test were subsequently removed after real-session prevalence showed zero useful text interceptions and seven harmful image interceptions.

bugs.error_message: Cross-project prevalence artifact verification was first run from customopenwolf with Context Doctor-relative paths, producing three ENOENT failures.
bugs.root_cause: I ignored the existing cross-project command rule and used paths relative to Context Doctor without changing cwd or supplying absolute paths, so Bash correctly resolved them against the driving customopenwolf repository.
bugs.fix: Reran both hash and JSON inspections with absolute Context Doctor paths, matched all three published SHA-256 values, and bound the QA record to the authoritative snapshot. Future cross-project commands must use absolute paths or an explicit npm --prefix/cd compound command.

bugs.error_message: Missing atomicWriteJson import silently disabled all pre-write lesson-hit persistence.
bugs.root_cause: recordLessonHit called atomicWriteJson without importing it. @ts-nocheck and syntax-only self-checks accepted the unbound identifier, and the hook's fail-open try/catch swallowed the ReferenceError after still emitting its warning.
bugs.fix: Import atomicWriteJson in source, source-adjacent runtime, portable template, and installed hook; add a production-bound regression that asserts cerebrum-stats.json is written and goes red when the import is removed.

bugs.error_message: Nested QA ignore verification passed vacuously because the repository root ignore policy masked the shipped nested policy defect.
bugs.root_cause: The nested policy used qa/*.md, which did not independently match qa/nested/reduction.md. The verifier ran inside this repository, whose root .gitignore already matched .wolf/qa/**/*.md, so the unrelated parent rule satisfied the assertion.
bugs.fix: Use qa/**/*.md in every nested-policy surface and test it in a fresh Git repository containing only the shipped .wolf/.gitignore, including durable-template negative assertions and a broken-pattern control.

bugs.error_message: Isolated nested-ignore regression still inherited user-global Git excludes and could pass with no shipped policy.
bugs.root_cause: A fresh git init removed repository-parent policy but git check-ignore still consulted core.excludesFile. A hostile global **/reduction.md pattern satisfied every positive and durable-exception assertion even when .wolf/.gitignore was absent.
bugs.fix: Create a known-empty excludes file and pass -c core.excludesFile=<that file> to every check-ignore invocation. A disconnected-policy control now exits 1 despite hostile global config, while removing the override reproduces the old false pass.

bugs.error_message: Nested-ignore regression covered the source template but not the independently maintained embedded init fallback.
bugs.root_cause: The source .gitignore and generateTemplate embedded fallback are separate producers, but the first regression copied only src/templates/.gitignore. A fallback-only recursive-pattern regression would therefore ship with the test green.
bugs.fix: Import the built init runtime, generate the embedded .gitignore through production generateTemplate(), and run the same isolated Git assertions for both producers. Reverting only the built fallback to qa/*.md now exits 1 on the nested path.

bugs.error_message: Missing required overwrite templates were replaced with zero-byte generated fallbacks during init.
bugs.root_cause: writeTemplateFile routed every missing non-OPENWOLF template to generateTemplate, whose unknown-key fallback is an empty string. PROTOCOL-UPGRADE-2026-06.md and reframe-frameworks.md are ALWAYS_OVERWRITE but had no embedded entries, so package-layout drift erased installed content.
bugs.fix: Allow embedded generation only for .gitignore; throw for every other missing required template before writing. A built-runtime regression supplies empty template storage and proves both installed protocol files retain exact bytes.

bugs.error_message: Embedded nested gitignore fallback had drifted from the canonical template and silently dropped five policies.
bugs.root_cause: The hand-maintained embedded .gitignore omitted logs/, **/logs/, !experiments/, !experiments/*.json, and experiments/artifacts/ while its comment claimed it mirrored src/templates/.gitignore.
bugs.fix: Synchronize the complete canonical policy into the embedded fallback and assert byte equality between generated built-runtime fallback and src/templates/.gitignore before semantic checks. Removing two fallback-only rules now drives the test red.

bugs.error_message: Clean release-only commit test failed: currentSessionId is not a function; Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'review-0001')
bugs.root_cause: The first release-only commit excluded modified nudge state and command files that the newly committed production-bound tests and review completion runtime depend on, so the commit was not a closed reproducible unit even though the dirty working tree passed.
bugs.fix: Include the reviewed nudge state runtime/source/template, nudge command, and its production-bound safety test in the release commit closure; rerun the full suite from a fresh detached worktree.

bugs.error_message: Fleet update run from a detached release worktree updated the canonical customopenwolf source checkout instead of skipping it.
bugs.root_cause: Source-project exclusion compared each registry root only with the running worktree realpath (or the legacy exact name openwolf), so another checkout of the same source repository was treated as an ordinary managed project.
bugs.fix: Recognize another source checkout by matching the running package identity plus the source-only src/cli/update.ts and templates/wolf layout markers; retain negative controls for ordinary same-name and different-package projects.

bugs.error_message: Initializing markerless mt5_dgm_lite selected and updated the ancestor /mnt/j/projectshome/projects WolfPack root.
bugs.root_cause: init exposed no exact-root option, so findProjectRoot climbed to the ancestor .wolf marker and interpreted a successful parent upgrade as the requested nested initialization.
bugs.fix: Add openwolf init --root <path>, validate that the exact path is an existing directory before writes, and test a markerless child beneath a parent .wolf sentinel with an isolated registry.

bugs.error_message: Initial fleet verifier reported 672 managed-file mismatches after a successful rollout.
bugs.root_cause: The ad hoc verifier compared installed OPENWOLF.md with templates/wolf and installed hook JavaScript with source-adjacent mirrors, while update actually installs src/templates bytes and freshly built dist/src hook bytes.
bugs.fix: Bind rollout verification to the producer paths actually used by update.ts; rerun across all non-source targets and require protected hashes, managed hashes, registrations, and versions to match.
